resources.string:
BentoBar draws your items (network speed, timer, calendar, tools…) on the status bar. Android allows that only through an accessibility service.

With it on, BentoBar: reads only the status bar's layout, to find free space for your items; reads the colour of the status bar clock, so your items match it; and runs the system actions you pick in the Tools menu or as a Shortcut item, such as screenshot or lock.

It doesn't read other apps' windows or watch your keyboard, mouse or touches. Nothing the service reads ever leaves your Googlebook: BentoBar never collects or shares it.

BentoBar goes online for two items only, and only after you set them up: Weather asks Open-Meteo about the city you search for, and Flight asks AirLabs about the flight you enter, with a key of your own. BentoBar sends nothing else anywhere: not your layout, your calendar, what\'s playing or anything it measures. It has no accounts of its own, no ads and no analytics, and it sends its developer nothing. Its accessibility service reads only the status bar (its layout and its clock\'s colour), never other apps. With Usage access on, it also reads how much data and storage each app uses, for the Network and Storage menus, and nothing else.

Weather sends Open-Meteo the city you search for. For the forecast it sends the coordinates of the city you pick, rounded to about a kilometre: about every 30 minutes while the bar is on screen, and when you open its menu or press Refresh. Open-Meteo sees your IP address, as any website does, and may keep it in its logs for 90 days.
